Package com.jwoglom.pumpx2.pump.messages.response.historyLog

Class ControlResponseHistoryLog

java.lang.Object
com.jwoglom.pumpx2.pump.messages.response.historyLog.HistoryLog
com.jwoglom.pumpx2.pump.messages.response.historyLog.ControlResponseHistoryLog
public class ControlResponseHistoryLog extends HistoryLog
The response the pump sent to a signed CONTROL request, written immediately after the ControlRequestHistoryLog for that request (its requestOpCode is this record's responseOpCode minus one in 3692/3692 records across both capture sets).

The class name is provisional: Tandem's cloud export and the Mobi app's HistoryLogType enum do not name this opcode.

Only some commands are answered with this record. Observed response opcodes: 133 UserInteraction, 135 SetMaxBolusLimit, 137 SetMaxBasalLimit, 155 ResumePumping, 157 SuspendPumping, 167 StopTempRate, 195 CgmHighLowAlert, 197 CgmRiseFallAlert, 199 CgmOutOfRangeAlert, 211 SetQuickBolusSettings, 213 SetPumpAlertSnooze, 215 ChangeTimeDate, 217 SetBgReminder, 221 SetSiteChangeReminder, 223 SetLowInsulinAlert, 225 SetAutoOffAlert, 229 SetPumpSounds, 237 SetActiveIDP and 245 PlaySound. SetTempRate is answered with SetTempRateResponseHistoryLog instead; the cartridge/fill commands and DismissNotification use other opcodes as well.

Byte 11 and bytes 13-25 are zero in every Mobi record examined; they are kept as raw accessors. See https://github.com/jwoglom/pumpx2/issues/145.

    • getStatus

      public int getStatus()
      The status byte of that response: 0 on success. Every nonzero value checked against the app log matched a response that reported a failure (for example a ResumePumping request rejected with status 1 and retried successfully a second later); StopTempRate responses logged as successful all read 0 here (1734/1734).
      Returns:
      the response status, 0 for success

    • getUnknownTail

      public byte[] getUnknownTail()
      Bytes 13-25. They are zero on the Mobi. In 17 t:slim X2 records answering UserInteraction (response opcode 133), bytes 15-17 of the record (index 2-4 here) held the low 24 bits of the record's own pumpTimeSec; their purpose is unknown.
      Returns:
      a copy of bytes 13-25
